newsitem.title: CHINA: China court rejects appeal of dissident.
newsitem.headline: China court rejects appeal of dissident.

text.p: A Chinese court has rejected an appeal by dissident Li Hai and upheld his nine-year jail term for prying into state secrets, a Hong Kong-based human rights watchdog group said on Thursday.
The Beijing Intermediate People's Court recently rejected Li's appeal, the group quoted the dissident's mother, Gong Liwen, as saying. The group did not say why it was rejected.

Li, 42, was found guilty of prying into state secrets after collecting information about political prisoners, his mother said, adding that she could not understand why this consititued prying into state secrets.
Li was initially charged with leaking state secrets but his family and lawyer challenged the charges, arguing that he was not a civil servant and had no access to state secrets.
Instead, Beijing's Chaoyang District Court, in a trial held behind closed doors, sentenced Li to nine years in prison last December for prying into state secrets.
Li was first arrested in May 1990 for his role in the 1989 student demonstrations for democracy that were crushed by the military with heavy loss of life.
He was released six months later and expelled from the philosophy department of the prestigious Beijing University, where he was a graduate student.
In its annual report on human rights, the U.S. State Department accused Beijing of effectively silencing public dissent in 1996 through jailings, intimidation or exile.
China considers criticism of its human rights record as interference in its internal affairs.
